name: US penny
headline: diameter
subtitle: Lincoln one-cent coin, copper-plated zinc
description: The one-cent coin, or penny, was one of the first coins made by the U.S. Mint after 1792 and shows President Lincoln on the front. Today's penny is copper-plated zinc, 19.05 mm across and 1.52 mm thick, and weighs 2.50 g. The Mint struck its final circulating penny on November 12, 2025, but the coin remains legal tender.

measures.label: Weight
measures.note: Official specification, stated as 2.50 g (0.088 oz)

facts.text: The penny is 97.5% zinc and 2.5% copper, with a plain edge.
The final circulating penny was struck in Philadelphia on November 12, 2025, ending a 232-year production run.
The cost of making each penny rose from 1.42 cents to 3.69 cents over the preceding decade, and an estimated 300 billion pennies remain in circulation.

sources.title: United States Mint Hosts Historic Ceremonial Strike for Final Production of the Circulating One-Cent Coin (press release, November 12, 2025)

caveats: Specifications are those the Mint lists for the current copper-plated zinc penny; older pennies made of other metals are not covered.
